name: Libya
summary: A North African country, an Italian colony until the Second World War, independent as a kingdom in 1951, ruled by Muammar Gaddafi from 1969 to 2011, and divided by civil war since.

knownFor.label: Leptis Magna
knownFor.note: Ruins of a great Roman city on the coast.

knownFor.label: Great Man-Made River
knownFor.note: Pipelines carrying underground water from the Sahara to the coast.

knownFor.label: Omar Mukhtar
knownFor.note: Leader of resistance to Italian rule, executed in 1931; a national hero.

location.value: North Africa, between Egypt and Tunisia; almost 1.8 million km², mostly covered by the Libyan Desert.

terrain.value: A narrow coastal strip and a vast desert.

climate.value: Mediterranean on the coast, extremely dry inland.

resources.value: Africa’s largest proven oil reserves; underground fossil water.

disasters.value: The Derna dam collapse after Storm Daniel (2023) killed thousands.

population.value: About 1.54 million in 1964; about 6.7 million today.

urbanisation.value: About 90% of people live along the coast, mostly in Tripoli, Benghazi and Misrata.

disease.value: Hospitals and clinics were damaged by the wars of 2011 and 2014 onward.

migration.value: Migrant workers from Africa and Asia; a route for migrants to Europe.

economicBase.value: Oil exports, beginning after oil was discovered in 1959, make up most of the state’s income.

tradeRoutes.value: Oil and gas are sent through Mediterranean ports to Europe, and migrants cross the desert and sea.

wealth.value: Rich in oil, but damaged by conflict and with uneven income.

moneyAndTax.value: The Libyan dinar; the state controls most income through oil revenue.

inequality.value: Oil wealth controlled by those in power.

governmentType.value: A kingdom (1951–69), then a republic under Gaddafi, called the Jamahiriya from 1977; rival governments after 2011.

succession.value: King Idris was overthrown by a coup in 1969; Gaddafi ruled until the uprising of 2011, and since then rival governments have competed.

institutions.value: Very weak since 2011, with rival governments in the east and west.

eliteConflict.value: Rival governments in Tripoli and the east.

armyAndTech.value: Rival militias and forces loyal to different governments and commanders.

majorWars.value: The 2011 civil war and NATO intervention; second civil war (2014–20).

territoryChange.value: The borders drawn in the colonial era remain the same, apart from the Aouzou Strip, which Libya held from 1973 to 1994.

alliancesRivals.value: Shifting foreign backers, including Turkey, Russia, Egypt and the United Arab Emirates, have supported rival sides since 2014.

inventions.value: The Great Man-Made River, the world’s largest irrigation project, pipes underground water from the south to the cities.

scienceEducation.value: Free education and rising literacy under Gaddafi.

openness.value: Closed under Muammar Gaddafi, with restricted travel and media; more open but unstable since 2011.

communicationTransport.value: Coastal highways link the main towns; there are few railways.

religion.value: Sunni Islam is practised by almost all Libyans.

artsArchitecture.value: Roman and Greek ruins; Gaddafi’s Green Book (1975).

socialStructure.value: Tribal and regional loyalties, with a Berber (Amazigh) minority.

sharedIdentity.value: Three historic regions: Tripolitania, Cyrenaica and Fezzan.

dailyLife.value: Many people live in city apartments and eat couscous, bazin (barley dough) and tea.

neighbours.value: Egypt, Sudan, Chad, Niger, Algeria, Tunisia.

ideasReligions.value: Muammar Gaddafi’s “Third Universal Theory”, set out in the Green Book (1975–79), mixed socialism and Islam.

colonisation.value: An Italian colony (1911–43), then British and French administration.

riseSignals.value: Independence as a kingdom on 24 December 1951.

peakPeriod.value: The oil boom of the 1970s raised incomes and public spending sharply.

overallCertainty.value: Recent events and figures are disputed.
